extracted.intended_audience: teachers, school administrators, youth program coordinators, and parents looking for youth creative-writing workshops in the Denver area
extracted.subtask_description: Descriptions and program standards for Lighthouse Writers Workshop's Young Writers Workshops — in-person and virtual creative-writing offerings for grades 3–12, intended for schools, afterschool programs, camps, and outreach sites. Covers goals, formats, genres, activities, capacities, durations, pricing/accommodations, and customization options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program goal — foster creativity, self-expression, excitement about writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Lighthouse's Young Writers Workshops are designed to foster creativity, self-expression, and excitement about writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis is on enjoyment and engagement rather than grades: 'There are no grades here, just the stories.' Programs aim to make writing fun and empower students through storytelling; offered in-person and virtually, and across afterschool, weekend, and summer formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructional staffing — led by working, published writers
rubrics_metrics.description: Workshops are led by working, published writers with a passion for sharing their craft.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instructors actively engage young writers in craft, provide new tools for self-expression, and work to increase literacy and writing skills; author visits send 'a real, live writer' to classrooms to talk and write with students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access & outreach — provide programming across varied sites
rubrics_metrics.description: Offer outreach workshops to students across the Denver metro area, including schools, juvenile residential treatment centers, and collaborations with other arts organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs can be scheduled at Lighthouse or as field trips; outreach aims to increase access to innovative creative-writing programming.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skill-building objective — increase literacy and writing skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructors provide new tools for self-expression and increase literacy and writing skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Workshops combine reading, writing, listening, and sharing to build both creative and literacy competencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Customization to classroom/program goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Workshops are customized to fit individual classroom or program goals and existing school curriculum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Available formats include hour-long presentations, one-day or week-long intensives, after-school programs, multi-week sessions, or longer-term workshops that may culminate in public readings or published anthologies (or both), depending on needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genre & format coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Offerings cover a range of genres and formats including poetry, short story, novel, memoir, flash fiction, graphic novel, personal essay, screenwriting, and themed workshops (e.g., science fiction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Workshops may be tailored (e.g., Fiction Toolbox vs. Poetry Toolbox) and adapted to different age groups and skill levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workshop formats & durations
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple session lengths and formats are offered: single two-hour sessions, 90-minute sessions, 60-minute author visits, one-day or week-long intensives, multi-week or year-long programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Format chosen should match goals: shorter visits for introductions or author talks; multi-week programs for drafting, revision, and culminating public readings or anthologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hands-on, play-based craft activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Workshops incorporate hands-on activities and games to explore elements of craft and make writing fun.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sample activities include creating bizarre characters, making villains more interesting, drawing maps for new worlds, blackout and cut-and-paste poetry, writing scenes for TV shows, inventing words, and freewriting. All workshops include some reading, writing, listening, and sharing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learning outcomes — drafting, revision, editing, and sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: Workshops aim for concrete creative outputs: students draft, revise, edit, and share their work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Sci‑fi workshop promises students will 'leave the workshop with four drafts of sci‑fi originals'; Screenwriting Lab results range from at least a scene to full-length scripts depending on length of program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance & oral storytelling emphasis
rubrics_metrics.description: Some workshops focus on oral presentation and performance of writing (e.g., 'Make Your Words Sing').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These emphasize sharing stories aloud, experimenting with rhythm and sound, and using prompts to 'unleash stories that matter.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Memoir/personal essay technique using objects
rubrics_metrics.description: Exercises (e.g., Hermit Crab Essay) use objects from the real world as protective shells to help students tell vulnerable personal stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using an object (playlist, shoes, rooms, clothing sizes) allows students to deliver personal material in a safer framing, producing meaningful results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity and staffing ratios
rubrics_metrics.description: Each workshop lists recommended capacities and, when relevant, student-to-chaperone or student-to-chapbook ratios (e.g., 'Capacity 30 stu., 1 chap. per 4 stu.' for Screenwriting Lab).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capacity figures (15, 30, 300) should guide planning for group size, materials, and instructor attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grade/age targeting per offering
rubrics_metrics.description: Each workshop specifies applicable grade levels (examples include grades 3–8 for Creative Writing Lab; 3–12 across other offerings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose workshops appropriate to developmental level and grade-specified ranges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost & accommodations — reduced price and scholarships
rubrics_metrics.description: Pricing accommodations are available: reduced price for Title 1 schools and scholarships available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schools and programs should inquire about cost options; contact info is provided for arranging accommodations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Customization & contact process
rubrics_metrics.description: Workshops can be customized for particular schools, sites, students, and budgets; contact information is provided for scheduling and customization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To schedule or customize programming, contact designated emails (info@lighthousewriters.org or Roxanne@lighthousewriters.org) or visit the Lighthouse website/phone number listed.
